general.title: Getting Started
general.summary: Learn the NEXORIA website, server dashboard, modules, commands, verification, tickets, and account integrations.

sections.heading: Using NEXORIA
sections.body: Sign in with Discord, choose a server, and use the available server modules to manage NEXORIA features. The website also provides documentation, leaderboards, profile settings, and account integrations.

sections.heading: Server access
sections.body: Server availability and dashboard access are determined by the server's NEXORIA settings and your Discord permissions or configured server role access.

sections.heading: Documentation
sections.body: Use the documentation search to find a module, command, variable, setting, or feature. Module documentation is updated with the features currently exposed by NEXORIA.

general.title: Module System
general.summary: NEXORIA is organized into modules that add focused server features.

sections.heading: Available modules
sections.body: NEXORIA currently documents Custom Commands, Logging, Member Automation, Reaction Roles, Setup, Ticket Tool, Roblox Verification, and Webhooks.

sections.heading: Module settings
sections.body: Each server module has its own settings and data. Disabling a module hides its controls without requiring you to recreate the server configuration.

general.title: Account & Configuration
general.summary: Understand the public account and server settings available in NEXORIA.

sections.heading: Discord account
sections.body: Discord is used to sign in and identify which servers are available to you. You can manage connected Discord accounts from User Settings.

sections.heading: Email integration
sections.body: You can verify connected email addresses in User Settings. One connected email can be selected as your main email. Announcement emails are sent only to that verified main email when one is selected.

sections.heading: Roblox integration
sections.body: Connect Roblox accounts through NEXORIA User Settings. The account selected as Main Roblox is used where a feature needs a primary Roblox account, including server verification.

general.title: Status and Refreshing
general.summary: The dashboard continuously checks NEXORIA service status and shows the current bot uptime.

sections.heading: Status
sections.body: The status indicator shows whether NEXORIA is reachable and displays host count, latency, uptime, and server information when available.

sections.heading: Uptime
sections.body: Current uptime is calculated from the running bot process and is shown with hours, minutes, seconds, and milliseconds when those values are non-zero.

sections.heading: Connection recovery
sections.body: If one service host stops responding, the website stops repeatedly retrying that host and checks the other configured hosts. When a healthy host is available, normal dashboard requests continue through it.

general.title: Announcements
general.summary: NEXORIA announcements can be delivered through Discord and email notifications.

sections.heading: Discord announcements
sections.body: Official announcements can be published to the configured announcement destination and can notify the appropriate server recipients.

sections.heading: Email announcements
sections.body: Announcement emails are sent only to users who have a verified connected email selected as their Main email. Secondary connected emails are never included in announcement delivery. If a user has no verified main email, no announcement email is sent to that user.

general.title: Website & Navigation
general.summary: How the public NEXORIA website is organized.

sections.heading: Main Menu
sections.body: The Main Menu provides the bot invite, Dashboard, Support Server, Leaderboards, and other public navigation options.

sections.heading: Documentation
sections.body: Documentation is available from the website and is grouped into general topics and module references. Use search to find a specific feature.

sections.heading: Dashboard
sections.body: After signing in with Discord, choose a server to open its available modules and settings.

sections.heading: Leaderboards
sections.body: Leaderboards display data supplied by NEXORIA modules, such as support and verified-server statistics when those providers are available.

general.title: General Settings
general.summary: Server-owner controls for access, logging, announcements, and other server-wide behavior.

sections.heading: Dashboard access
sections.body: Server owners can choose who can access the dashboard for the server, including administrators or selected server roles where supported.

sections.heading: Audit Log access
sections.body: Audit Log access can be restricted according to the server's access settings.

sections.heading: Announcements
sections.body: Server owners can control whether official terminal announcements are delivered to that server.

sections.heading: Refresh settings
sections.body: Status and other live dashboard data can refresh automatically. The website keeps the refresh behavior responsive while avoiding unnecessary repeated requests.

general.title: Feature Reference
general.summary: A current overview of NEXORIA's main user-facing features.

sections.heading: Tickets
sections.body: Ticket Tool provides support panels, ticket subjects, staff claiming, closing messages, sharing, transcripts, ratings, and insights.

sections.heading: Logging
sections.body: Logging records Discord activity, message history, message deletions and edits, and other configured events. Message Archive can search stored message records independently of the Discord logging channel.

sections.heading: Roblox Verification
sections.body: Roblox Verification connects a member's Discord account with a connected Roblox account and applies the server's verification rules. The official verification channel and thread are maintained by NEXORIA while verification is enabled.

sections.heading: Custom Commands
sections.body: Custom Commands supports prefix and slash commands, visual advanced flows, variables, permissions, cooldowns, previews, listeners, and reusable templates.

modules.title: Ticket Tool
modules.summary: Support tickets: panels users click to open a ticket, per-subject settings, staff claiming, closing DMs, share links, and insights.

sections.heading: Panels
sections.body: A panel is a message (plain text and/or an embed) with buttons or a dropdown that users click to open a ticket. Each option on a panel connects to a Ticket Template (a "subject"), so one panel can offer several kinds of tickets at once.

sections.heading: Subjects (Ticket Templates)
sections.body: Each subject has its own welcome message, close message, staff roles, user/staff/claimer channel permissions, ticket limits, creation cooldowns, an optional auto-close timer, and its own logging toggles.

sections.heading: Claiming & Staff-Only Claim
sections.body: Staff can claim a ticket to signal they're handling it. When Staff-Only Claim is on, only members with a staff role for that subject can claim.

sections.heading: Closing DM
sections.body: A guild-wide, customizable embed DM sent to whoever opened a ticket once it's closed, separate from a subject's own plain-text close message. Supports {ticket.url} — a link back to the person's own authenticated ticket page.

sections.heading: Share Links
sections.body: When sharing is turned on, a closed ticket can be given a public, read-only share link so its transcript can be sent to someone without dashboard access.

sections.heading: Insights
sections.body: Ticket volume, close rate, and staff performance over a selectable time period, computed from real ticket data — nothing here is simulated.

modules.title: Custom Commands
modules.summary: Build prefix and slash commands with a visual node graph, branching conditions, roles, variables, Discord actions, a simulator, and execution controls. Basic mode is for simple responses; Advanced mode is a connected node editor for complete command logic.

sections.heading: Basic mode — quick commands
sections.body: Basic mode is for a straightforward trigger → response command. Choose Prefix or Slash, enter the trigger, add the response, choose who can run it, then save. Use Basic when the command only needs a small number of ordered actions and no visual branching.

sections.heading: Advanced mode — visual command flows
sections.body: Advanced mode opens an empty canvas for a new command. Add exactly one Trigger node, then connect its output to the first executable node. Nothing is inserted automatically. Existing commands are migrated into their graph without changing their saved behavior.

sections.heading: Every Advanced node
sections.body: Trigger — required entry node; sets command name, trigger, Prefix/Slash mode, scope, prefix, and slash description. Description — stores a separate slash-command description. Permissions — controls Everyone, Administrators, or selected roles. Send Message — sends plain Discord text with variables. Send Embed — sends a title/description/color embed. Reply — replies to the triggering message. Mention User — sends the command user's mention plus optional text. Add Role — adds a selected role to the user. Remove Role — removes a selected role. React — adds a reaction to the triggering message. DM User — sends the command user a direct message. Delete Trigger — deletes the prefix message that invoked the command. Wait — pauses execution for the selected delay. Stop — ends the flow immediately. If — flexible Target → Condition → Value/Role branching node. If Contains — checks trigger text for a substring. If Has Role — checks whether the user has a selected role. Random Chance — randomly chooses the True branch using a percentage. Comment — builder-only documentation note. Set Variable — creates or overwrites a temporary command variable. Change Variable — adds or subtracts a number from a variable. Log — writes a diagnostic message to the bot console.

sections.heading: Command nodes
sections.body: Trigger is required and defines the command name, trigger text, prefix/slash mode, scope, and slash description. Description stores a slash-command description when you want metadata separate from Trigger. Permissions controls Everyone, Administrators, or selected roles. These metadata nodes configure the command and are not sent to Discord as actions.

sections.heading: Discord action nodes
sections.body: Send Message sends normal text and supports documented variables. Send Embed creates a title, description, and color. Reply replies to the triggering message. Mention User adds the command user's mention. Add Role and Remove Role change a member's roles when the bot can manage the target role. React reacts to the triggering message. DM User sends a direct message. Delete Trigger removes the triggering prefix message when Discord permissions allow it.

sections.heading: Flow nodes
sections.body: Wait pauses execution for a controlled number of milliseconds. Stop ends execution immediately. Connect output ports directly to input ports; a normal input accepts one incoming connection. Wires move with nodes and can be selected and removed from the custom editor menu.

sections.heading: Logic and condition nodes
sections.body: If is the flexible condition node. Choose a Target such as User, Message, Channel, Command, or Variable, then choose the matching condition and value/role. User supports Has Role, Doesn't Have Role, Is Administrator, and Is Server Owner. Message supports Contains, Doesn't Contain, Equals, and Doesn't Equal. Channel can check text, thread, and forum types. Command can compare name or trigger. Variable compares a stored command variable. Random Chance branches by percentage. Branch nodes expose separate True and False outputs.

sections.heading: Variable nodes and custom variables
sections.body: Set Variable creates or overwrites a temporary command variable. Change Variable adds or subtracts a numeric amount. Custom variables can also be created in the command editor, edited, inserted into supported message fields, and deleted. Use {var.name} for custom command variables and the documented built-in variable names such as {user.mention}, {server.name}, {channel.name}, and {command.name}.

sections.heading: Utility nodes
sections.body: Log writes a diagnostic line to the bot console and is useful while debugging a flow. Comment is a builder-only note and never sends a Discord message. Use comments to explain why a branch or variable exists.

sections.heading: Preview, validation, and console
sections.body: Run opens the custom preview. It simulates a user invoking the command, shows bot replies as a conversation, evaluates branches, and records diagnostics. Preview runs do not change Discord. Nodes with missing required data receive a red problem outline. The console stays available between preview runs until Clear console is pressed.

sections.heading: Editing and navigation
sections.body: Drag a node header to move it. Drag directly from an output port to an input port to create a wire. Right-click inside the builder opens only the NEXORIA editor menu with relevant actions such as Duplicate, Center, Delete, Remove connection, and Add node here. Back and Exit both respect unsaved changes and ask before leaving. Use Cancel/Back to leave the editor without accidentally navigating outside the command workflow.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.body: Role gate: Trigger /staff → If (User → Has Role → Staff) → True → Add Role/Send Message; False → Send Message. Variable counter: Trigger ?count → Set Variable count=1 → Change Variable count +1 → Send Message "Count: {count}". Conditional text: Trigger ?hello → If (Message → Contains → hello) → True → Reply "Hello!"; False → Reply "Try saying hello.".

sections.heading: Built-in commands
sections.body: NEXORIA built-in commands are always available and cannot be disabled or deleted. Current built-ins are /dashboard, /help, /discord, /status, /verify, /unverify, /mute, and /unmute. Built-in commands are shown first; custom commands are listed after the built-in category.

sections.heading: Scope nodes — typed outputs
sections.body: Scope Input is a reusable typed output node. Choose Text, Full Trigger Message, Rest of Message, Command Argument, Quoted Text, Number, Boolean, URL, Emoji, Command User Mention, First User Mention in Message, User ID, User Name, Role Mention/ID, Channel Mention/ID, Trigger Text, Command Name, Server Name/ID, or time values. Argument and quoted scopes can choose an argument number. Every scope node has a stable node ID token such as {scope-node-id}. Connect its value output to an action and insert the token into supported fields; NEXORIA resolves it at execution time. Example: Trigger → Scope Input (Command Argument #1) → Send Message with `You entered {scope-node-id}`. Multiple scope outputs can feed different nodes, and one output can be referenced by multiple downstream fields.

sections.heading: Templates
sections.body: The Advanced builder includes reusable templates. Starter templates provide common patterns such as a welcome message, argument responder, and role gate. Save any graph as a named template with a description, then use it to create a new graph. Templates are stored for the server and reset command metadata such as the Trigger name so the same graph can be reused safely.

sections.heading: Advanced variable usage and locations
sections.body: The Advanced Variables manager shows each variable's current value, permissions, known node locations, and shared-server consumers. Click a variable to inspect every command/node that references it. Select a location to open that command and focus the exact node. Inside the Advanced builder, the Variables panel provides the same navigation. Shared variables continue to respect read/write exposure permissions; a connection without the required permission is treated as a node problem.

sections.heading: Output chaining
sections.body: Output nodes are first-class values. Connect a Scope Input or another output-producing node into a transform, condition, or action. Each output node has a stable token such as {node-id}. Message, embed, DM, log, variable, and compatible condition fields can resolve those tokens. One output can feed multiple downstream nodes, allowing a single captured value to be reused throughout a command.

modules.title: Logging
modules.summary: Server activity logging — pick a channel per log type (or per whole category), self-posted or via webhook, with ignore lists for noisy channels/roles/users.

sections.heading: Log types
sections.body: Grouped into categories (Bot, Custom Commands, Applications, Channels, Roles, Members, Messages, Voice, and more) — expand a category to set a channel for each type inside it individually, or set the whole category at once. Custom Command Used records custom command execution with the user, channel, and command name.

sections.heading: Self-post vs. webhook
sections.body: By default NEXORIA posts log messages itself. A channel can instead be set to use a webhook — useful for custom branding in that channel — but since anyone who obtains the webhook URL can post to it, this is opt-in per channel with a warning before you turn it on.

sections.heading: Ignore lists
sections.body: Channels, roles, and users can be excluded from logging entirely, so noisy bots or a specific channel don't flood your log channels.

modules.title: Nexoria Honeypot
modules.summary: Create visible trap channels that delete messages, apply a configurable punishment, optionally DM the user with a server invite, and record every trigger.

sections.heading: Honeypot channels
sections.body: Create multiple Honeypot text channels directly from the dashboard. NEXORIA places each new channel at a random position and tracks it by Discord channel ID, so renaming the channel does not break the trap. If the channel is deleted in Discord, it is removed from the dashboard automatically.

sections.heading: Punishments
sections.body: Choose Softban (Kick), Timeout, Ban, or Log Only. Timeout and temporary Ban durations are configurable. The triggered message is deleted before the configured action is applied. Server owners and administrators are protected from automatic punishment.

sections.heading: Trigger message
sections.body: Each Honeypot channel receives a NEXORIA-branded warning message with the current punishment and a live trigger count. The message includes Dashboard, Invite Bot, and Documentation buttons.

sections.heading: DM on trigger
sections.body: Optionally DM a triggered user with a NEXORIA-branded notice and an invite back to the server. Administrator example text is only included for administrator previews; administrators themselves are protected from automatic punishment.

sections.heading: Logging
sections.body: Honeypot Triggered is a normal Logging event. The Honeypot module can set its log channel directly, and that same channel is synchronized with Logging → Honeypot Triggered. If no Discord log channel is selected, the event can still be retained in the Logging history.

modules.title: Member Automation
modules.summary: Gateway, Welcomer and Leaver automation in one module.

sections.heading: Gateway & Welcomer
sections.body: Automatically assign a configured join role and send a customizable welcome message.

sections.heading: Leaver
sections.body: Send a customizable goodbye message with member ping and remaining member count.

modules.title: Reaction Roles
modules.summary: Send editable role-selection messages using reactions, buttons, or dropdowns.

sections.heading: Messages
sections.body: Create and edit messages after sending. NEXORIA keeps the message ID so changes update the existing Discord message.

sections.heading: Selection types
sections.body: Reactions support up to 20 role reactions. Buttons support up to 5 buttons. Dropdowns support up to 25 options.

sections.heading: Cooldowns
sections.body: A per-user message cooldown prevents rapid role switching.

modules.title: Webhooks
modules.summary: Create, customize and execute Discord webhooks.

sections.heading: Webhook control
sections.body: Create webhooks in text channels, change their names and avatars, choose channels, and send rich messages with embeds and mention controls.

modules.title: Roblox Verification
modules.summary: Official NEXORIA Roblox verification for server members.

sections.heading: How verification works
sections.body: Members use /verify in a server, choose the Roblox account connected to their NEXORIA identity, confirm the account, and complete verification. NEXORIA then applies the server's verification state and can remove the Unverified role.

sections.heading: Roblox Verification channel
sections.body: When verification is enabled, NEXORIA creates or uses the configured verification channel, posts its official verification information there, and opens a dedicated thread where members can use /verify.

sections.heading: Official message
sections.body: The official verification message is controlled by NEXORIA and cannot be edited from the dashboard. This keeps the message consistent and clearly identifies it as an official NEXORIA message.

sections.heading: Privacy
sections.body: Members can manage whether their Roblox username is shared with the server from the verification privacy controls.

modules.title: Server Setup
modules.summary: Configure a complete server baseline, copy a server structure, or import selected server settings.

sections.heading: Setup modes
sections.body: Full Server, roles, channels, permissions, logging and status can be applied independently.

sections.heading: Server Copy Board
sections.body: Export a structure-only NEXORIA snapshot containing server settings, roles, role permissions and hierarchy, channels, categories, channel permission overwrites, optional emojis/stickers, and NEXORIA module settings. Messages, ticket transcripts and logging history are never exported.

sections.heading: Import
sections.body: Paste a snapshot, load a JSON file, or paste it from the clipboard. You can choose whether to remove existing roles, channels, or expressions before importing, and can independently enable server settings and NEXORIA module settings. Role and channel IDs are remapped automatically so logging and module references continue to point at the imported structure.

sections.heading: Discord limitations
sections.body: Managed bot/integration roles and Discord-managed resources cannot be deleted or recreated by a bot and are therefore skipped. Discord permissions and any settings the bot lacks permission to change are applied on a best-effort basis.
